newsitem.title: UK: Euro oil swaps mixed - mogas down $1 but CFDs climb.
newsitem.headline: Euro oil swaps mixed - mogas down $1 but CFDs climb.

text.p: European oil swaps were mixed on Friday with Brent crude CFDs firmer but most oil products weaker, traders said.
Brent CFDs climbed about five cents a barrel for next week to 23 cents under July. The following three weeks ended around 18 cents, 18 cents and 19 cents under respectively.
Heavy fuel slipped $1 a tonne to $85 on June but low sulphur remained well supported from the United States and traded $10.50 higher.

Dealers said the contango remained steeply curved, reflecting downward pressure on nearby periods from summer exports of Russian fuel. The third to fourth quarter contango was assessed by brokers at $6 a tonne while the fourth to first quarter was an unusually wide nearer $4.
Gasoline slipped $1 a tonne to $204.00 for June but July traded $5.00 lower a couple of time and August talked a further $3.50 lower.

Gas oil crack spreads held at $4.30 a barrel (3Q97), $4.85 (4Q97) and $4.75 (1Q98). EN590 traded at $10.00 a tonne above the IPE while 0.2 percent traded at $3.25 a tonne over. -- Sam Arnold-Forster, London Newsroom +44 171 542 4984
